top.title: Mars Curiosity rover discovers massive field of polygons
top.summary: The surface of Mars is home to some of the most breathtaking and awe-inspiring landscapes in the solar system. This is primarily because the Red Planet lacks several resurfacing processes that Earth possesses, including plate tectonics, volcanism and flowing water.

top.title: AI mapping reveals hidden stage of Arctic freeze with climate implications
top.summary: As autumn gives way to winter across the Arctic, the ground doesn't immediately freeze solid. Instead, soils often linger near the freezing point for days or even weeks in a phase called the zero curtain. In a new NASA-led study, researchers produced high-resolution maps of the Arctic zero curtain.

top.title: Near-total lunar eclipse is coming up with the Americas in prime position
top.summary: Now it's the moon's turn to pull a disappearing act. After being shut out of this month's total solar eclipse, the Americas will have the best seats in the celestial house when Earth's shadow briefly envelops the moon. Almost the entire lunar surface will be masked Thursday night into Friday—a whopping 96%—making this an especially deep partial eclipse.

top.title: JWST finds early galaxies may be 4 times more massive than thought
top.summary: Astronomers using JWST have discovered that massive early galaxies contain far more small, faint stars than expected. That hidden population could make some of these galaxies three to four times more massive than previous estimates. The finding makes it even harder to explain how enormous, mature galaxies formed so soon after the Big Bang.

top.title: This yeast supplement may boost cancer-fighting immunity

more.title: Multilingual people may have brains up to 13 years younger

more.title: Animal genomes follow irreversible 'evolutionary highways' across thousands of species
more.summary: A human, an octopus, and a coral could hardly look more different—yet deep inside their cells, their chromosomes still carry recognizable pieces of a genome inherited from an animal ancestor that lived more than 600 million years ago. Since then, their chromosomes have fused, split and rearranged countless times. Today, thousands of animal genomes have been sequenced.

more.title: Earth's magnetosphere might not protect us from superstorms after all
